bounds: One reviewed in-app transfer, one pending row and one browser history entry. One atomic final admission wins against cancellation. History removal after publication admission preserves the file if the provider commits it.

The JVM probe runs the actual BrowserDownloads final copy, list removal, private removal and destruction methods with an in-memory provider and exact BrowserDownloadPolicy.History. It includes cancellation on a different thread during provider update and a commit followed by a lost acknowledgement.

The model excludes HTTP, captured files and OS DownloadManager transfers. JVM conformance checks the captured-file path separately. The model distinguishes a committed file with a lost acknowledgement from an acknowledged save. Failures of the conditional deletion operation itself, process death, Android MediaStore behavior and wall-clock limits are outside the model.

assumptions: Weak fairness of pending provider result or cancellation cleanup. Provider update may succeed or fail and owned-row cleanup is acknowledged.
